As of 229 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Our coastal low, centered just off Cape Cod, MA as of 
2AM, will finally begin to pull east as ridging over the Canadian 
Maritimes breaks down. Subsidence will begin to erode precipitation 
across the area toward this morning, with gradual drying in the mid 
to upper levels of the atmosphere. Low level moisture, however, will 
take a bit longer to depart due to continued easterly cyclonic flow. 
Low clouds will hang around the region, keeping mountains obscured, 
and temperatures on the seasonably cool side. Highs today as a 
result will be in the upper 50s to low 60s with weak diurnal 
heating. As clouds slowly erode from west to east, areas across the 
St. Lawrence Valley may be able to warm into the mid 60s, should 
clouds trend more sunny towards the latter portion of the day. Winds 
across the area today will be northerly and generally light. 
However, some continued channeled flow in the Champlain Valley will 
continue through this morning, before our pressure field becomes 
more broad this evening.

An airmass change will take place into the rest of the mid week 
period, as tropical moisture from the SW CONUS begin to advect 
northeastward. Ridging will build in across the Mississippi Valley 
and extend into our neck of the woods leading to warming 
temperatures with southerly flow Wednesday. Highs will warm into the 
upper 60s to low 70s Wednesday. Aside from some mid to high clouds, 
Wednesday looks to be fairly tranquil.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A brief pattern change will take place by the latter 
portion of the week as shower chances and warm temperatures return 
to the region, associated with Pacific tropical air. Zonal flow 
Thursday will turn more amplified to the southwest by Friday, 
advecting warm air and higher dewpoints in the region. 850-mb 
temperatures in the GFS and ECMWF are fairly consistent in the mid 
teens, supporting temperatures in the mid 70s for most locations. 
Complicating our maximum temperature potential Thursday will be the 
presence of advected low level moisture and potential shower 
activity. Decent isentropic lift along a boundary in the St. 
Lawrence Valley Thursday will spur shower chances by late Thursday 
into Friday. Model trends have hinted at delaying the arrival of 
shower chances towards Thursday night into Friday, keeping most of 
Thursday on the drier side. However, by Friday a cold front will 
push through the region with elevated PWs up to 1.5"; more 
reminiscent of a summer-time airmass. Thankfully, this front will be 
quite progressive, aided by a 40-50kt LLJ, and good stretching 
between a Bermuda high, and a building high across the Midwest. As a 
result, ensembles depict only a few tenths of an inch of rain, 
mainly across northern New York and northern Vermont. Only a 10-20% 
chance of exceeding 1" of rain exists in the GEFS, and is focused 
only over the St. Lawrence Valley. 

As our flow pattern turns more southwesterly on Thursday, our 
gradient flow will tighten with localized gusty winds. Soundings 
depict gusty channeled flow in the Champlain Valley winds with 
reasonable winds in the 25-30+ MPH range. Across northern New York, 
slightly stronger channeled flow is expected with winds approaching 
40 MPH in a reasonable higher end scenario out ahead of the cold 
front during the day Thursday. Given climatology, sustained winds 
look marginally strong in this area but gusts will not be impactful. 
Mountain summits will likely remain gusty around 40 MPH Thursday 
through mid day Friday. Winds look to weaken through the day
Friday with the arrival of better precipitation chances. 

KEY MESSAGE 3: A seasonable and dry start to the weekend is expected 
for Saturday as a brief period of high pressure builds into the 
region. The dry conditions look rather short lived, with 
precipitation chances increasing for Sunday as another low pressure 
system moves into the region. There is still some uncertainty 
regarding the low track at this point, which will influence how much 
precipitation we see, but additional rainfall chances look likely at 
this point. Temperatures this weekend look to be fairly seasonable, 
with daytime highs climbing into the upper 50s to mid 60s. Heading 
into next week, high pressure looks to build into the region again, 
bring dry weather and cooler temperatures.
